name: London
fact: Big Ben is really the name of the great bell inside the clock tower, not of the tower itself.

name: Paris
fact: The Eiffel Tower was built as the entrance arch for the 1889 World's Fair and was meant to stand for only twenty years.

name: Rome
fact: The coins tourists throw into the Trevi Fountain are collected and given to charity.

name: Venice
fact: St Mark's Campanile collapsed in 1902 and was rebuilt exactly as it had been, reopening in 1912.

name: Florence
fact: Brunelleschi's dome, finished in the 1430s, is still the largest brick dome ever built.

name: Milan
fact: Leonardo da Vinci's Last Supper is painted on a wall of the convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie, not on canvas.

name: Naples
fact: Teatro di San Carlo, opened in 1737, is the oldest opera house in Europe still in use.

name: Pisa
fact: The tower began to lean while it was still being built in the 12th century, because the ground under one side is soft.

name: Madrid
fact: The Temple of Debod is a real ancient Egyptian temple, given to Spain by Egypt and rebuilt stone by stone in a Madrid park.

name: Barcelona
fact: Gaudí's Sagrada Família has been under construction since 1882.

name: Seville
fact: The Giralda bell tower began as the minaret of the city's great mosque in the 12th century.

name: Granada
fact: The Alhambra was the palace of the Nasrid sultans, the last Muslim rulers in Spain, until 1492.

name: Valencia
fact: After a deadly flood in 1957 the Turia river was diverted, and its old bed became a long park through the city.

name: Berlin

landmarks.n: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe

fact: The East Side Gallery is the longest surviving stretch of the Berlin Wall, painted by artists from many countries in 1990.

name: Munich
fact: Surfers ride a standing wave all year round on the Eisbach, a stream running through the English Garden.

name: Cologne
fact: Work on the cathedral began in 1248, and its twin spires were finished only in 1880, more than 600 years later.

name: Hamburg
fact: Miniatur Wunderland in the Speicherstadt is the largest model railway in the world.

name: Dresden
fact: The Frauenkirche was destroyed in the bombing of 1945 and rebuilt between 1994 and 2005, partly from its original stones.

name: Amsterdam
fact: The ring of canals dug in the 17th century is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Prague
fact: The Astronomical Clock was first installed in 1410 and is the oldest astronomical clock still working.

name: Vienna
fact: The Riesenrad in the Prater, built in 1897, is one of the oldest Ferris wheels still turning.

name: Salzburg
fact: Mozart was born in 1756 in the yellow house at Getreidegasse 9, which is now a museum.

name: Budapest
fact: The Chain Bridge, opened in 1849, was the first permanent bridge across the Danube between Buda and Pest.

name: Athens
fact: The Panathenaic Stadium is built entirely of marble and hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896.

name: Lisbon
fact: The Santa Justa Lift, opened in 1902, still carries passengers up from the Baixa to the Carmo district.

name: Porto
fact: The Dom Luís I Bridge was designed by Théophile Seyrig, a former partner of Gustave Eiffel.

name: Dublin
fact: The Book of Kells, an illuminated gospel book made around the year 800, is on display at Trinity College.

name: Edinburgh
fact: Arthur's Seat, the hill rising over the city, is the remains of an extinct volcano.

name: Liverpool
fact: The Beatles played the Cavern Club nearly 300 times in the early 1960s.

name: Oxford
fact: The Ashmolean, opened in 1683, is the oldest public museum in Britain.

name: Nice
fact: The Promenade des Anglais is named after the English residents who paid for the first seafront path in the 1820s.

name: Marseille
fact: The Château d'If is the island prison where Alexandre Dumas locked up the hero of The Count of Monte Cristo.

name: Lyon
fact: The city's traboules are passageways running through buildings, which silk workers used to carry their cloth out of the rain.

name: Brussels
fact: The Atomium, built for the 1958 World's Fair, shows an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times.

name: Bruges
fact: The Church of Our Lady holds Michelangelo's Madonna and Child, one of the few works of his to leave Italy in his lifetime.

name: Copenhagen
fact: Tivoli Gardens, opened in 1843, is one of the oldest amusement parks in the world.

name: Stockholm
fact: The warship Vasa sank on its maiden voyage in 1628 and was raised almost intact in 1961.

name: Oslo
fact: The Nobel Peace Prize is presented in Oslo City Hall, while the other Nobel prizes are given in Stockholm.

name: Helsinki
fact: Temppeliaukio Church was carved directly into solid rock and opened in 1969.

name: Reykjavik
fact: The columns of Hallgrímskirkja were designed to look like the basalt lava columns found across Iceland.

name: Moscow
fact: St Basil's Cathedral was built in the 1550s on the orders of Ivan the Terrible to celebrate the capture of Kazan.

name: St Petersburg

landmarks.n: Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood

fact: The city was called Leningrad from 1924 until 1991, when its residents voted to bring back its old name.

name: Istanbul
fact: The Basilica Cistern was built under Emperor Justinian in the sixth century to store water for the city's palaces.

name: Krakow
fact: Every hour a trumpeter plays a call from the tower of St Mary's Basilica and breaks off mid-tune, recalling a trumpeter said to have been shot by an arrow.

name: Warsaw
fact: The Old Town was almost entirely destroyed in 1944 and rebuilt after the war, partly from 18th-century paintings by Bernardo Bellotto.

name: Bratislava
fact: St Martin's Cathedral was the coronation church of the Kingdom of Hungary for more than 250 years.

name: Ljubljana
fact: Many of the city's landmarks, including the two side spans of the Triple Bridge, are the work of the architect Jože Plečnik.

name: Zagreb
fact: A cannon is fired from Lotrščak Tower every day at noon.

name: Dubrovnik
fact: Many scenes of King's Landing in Game of Thrones were filmed in the old town and at Fort Lovrijenac.

name: Belgrade
fact: Kalemegdan fortress stands on the ridge where the Sava flows into the Danube.

name: Bucharest
fact: The Palace of the Parliament, begun under Ceausescu in the 1980s, is one of the largest and heaviest buildings in the world.

name: Sofia
fact: The Rotunda of St George, a Roman brick church from the fourth century, is thought to be the oldest building in the city.

name: Tallinn
fact: St Olaf's Church is said to have been the tallest building in the world in the 16th century.

name: Riga
fact: About a third of the buildings in the city centre are Art Nouveau, one of the largest collections of the style anywhere.

name: Vilnius
fact: Užupis declared itself an independent republic in 1997, an artists' joke complete with its own constitution.

name: Kyiv
fact: The Pechersk Lavra was founded in 1051 by monks who lived in caves dug into the hillside, and its cave passages can still be visited.

name: Valletta
fact: St John's Co-Cathedral holds Caravaggio's Beheading of Saint John the Baptist, the only painting he ever signed.

name: Bern
fact: Albert Einstein worked out his special theory of relativity in 1905 while living in a flat on Kramgasse, now the Einstein House.

name: Zurich
fact: The stained glass windows of the Fraumünster were made by Marc Chagall.

name: Geneva
fact: The Jet d'Eau began in the 19th century as a pressure valve for the city's hydraulic power network.

name: Monaco
fact: Grace Kelly, the American film star who became Princess of Monaco, is buried in Saint Nicholas Cathedral.

name: Tokyo
fact: Senso-ji in Asakusa is the city's oldest temple, traditionally said to have been founded in the 7th century.

name: Kyoto
fact: The paths of Fushimi Inari Taisha are lined with thousands of vermilion torii gates, each one donated by a person or a business.

name: Osaka
fact: The Glico Running Man sign over the Dotonbori canal has advertised a candy maker since the 1930s.

name: Hiroshima
fact: The Atomic Bomb Dome was one of the few buildings left standing near the hypocenter of the 1945 bombing and has been kept as a ruin ever since.

name: Nara
fact: Todai-ji's Great Buddha Hall, which houses a giant bronze Buddha, is one of the largest wooden buildings in the world.

name: Beijing
fact: The Forbidden City was home to the Ming and Qing emperors for nearly 500 years.

name: Shanghai
fact: Most of the grand buildings along the Bund were built by foreign banks and trading houses in the early 20th century.

name: Hong Kong
fact: The Peak Tram has been carrying passengers up the steep slopes of Victoria Peak since 1888.

name: Xi'an
fact: The Terracotta Army was discovered in 1974 by farmers digging a well.

name: Chengdu
fact: The city is the capital of Sichuan, the province where most of the world's wild giant pandas live.

name: Seoul
fact: Gyeongbokgung was built in 1395 as the main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty.

name: Busan
fact: Haedong Yonggungsa is a Buddhist temple built on the rocks right at the edge of the sea.

name: Bangkok
fact: The Reclining Buddha at Wat Pho is 46 meters long and covered in gold leaf.

name: Chiang Mai
fact: The great chedi of Wat Chedi Luang was damaged by an earthquake in the 16th century and has never been fully rebuilt.

name: Singapore
fact: The Merlion, half lion and half fish, was designed in 1964 as an emblem for the tourism board.

name: Kuala Lumpur
fact: The Petronas Towers were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.

name: Hanoi
fact: The Temple of Literature, founded in 1070 and dedicated to Confucius, was home to Vietnam's first national university.

name: Ho Chi Minh City
fact: On 30 April 1975 a North Vietnamese tank crashed through the gates of the Reunification Palace, ending the Vietnam War.

name: Delhi
fact: Qutub Minar, begun around 1200, is one of the tallest brick minarets in the world at about 73 meters.

name: Mumbai
fact: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, finished in 1888, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and still one of the busiest railway stations in India.

name: Agra
fact: The emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

name: Jaipur
fact: The many small windows of the Hawa Mahal let royal women watch life on the street without being seen.

name: Varanasi
fact: Manikarnika Ghat on the Ganges is the city's main cremation ground, where funeral pyres are said to burn day and night.

name: Kolkata
fact: Howrah Bridge, opened in 1943, is a cantilever bridge held together by rivets, with no nuts and bolts.

name: Amritsar
fact: The community kitchen of the Golden Temple serves free meals to tens of thousands of visitors every day.

name: Dubai
fact: Burj Khalifa has been the tallest building in the world since it opened in 2010.

name: Abu Dhabi
fact: The main prayer hall of the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque is laid with one of the largest hand-knotted carpets in the world.

name: Doha
fact: The Museum of Islamic Art was designed by I. M. Pei, the architect of the glass pyramid at the Louvre.

name: Jerusalem
fact: The Dome of the Rock, finished around 691, is one of the oldest surviving works of Islamic architecture.

name: Tel Aviv
fact: The White City, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, holds thousands of Bauhaus and International Style buildings from the 1930s.

name: Beirut
fact: Pigeon Rocks are two huge rock arches standing in the sea off the Raouche district.

name: Tehran
fact: Azadi Tower was built in 1971 to mark 2,500 years of the Persian Empire.

name: Isfahan
fact: Naqsh-e Jahan Square, laid out around 1600 by Shah Abbas I, is one of the largest city squares in the world.

name: Samarkand
fact: Gur-e-Amir is the mausoleum of the 14th-century conqueror Timur.

name: Kathmandu
fact: Boudhanath is one of the largest stupas in the world.

name: Manila
fact: Binondo, established in 1594, is often called the oldest Chinatown in the world.

name: Jakarta
fact: Istiqlal Mosque is the largest mosque in Southeast Asia, and it stands across the street from the city's Catholic cathedral.

name: Taipei
fact: The National Palace Museum holds treasures of the old imperial collection that were shipped over from the mainland in 1948 and 1949.

name: Phnom Penh
fact: Wat Phnom stands on the small hill that, according to legend, gave the city its name.

name: Siem Reap
fact: Ta Prohm has been left with huge silk-cotton and strangler fig trees growing out of its ruins.

name: Yangon
fact: The stupa of Shwedagon Pagoda is covered in gold plates, and its tip is set with thousands of diamonds and other gems.

name: Colombo
fact: The Lotus Tower, opened in 2019, is the tallest self-supported structure in South Asia.

name: Mecca
fact: Muslims all over the world face the Kaaba when they pray.

name: Riyadh
fact: Ibn Saud's capture of Masmak Fortress in 1902 was the first step towards founding modern Saudi Arabia.

name: Muscat
fact: The Al Jalali and Al Mirani forts were built by the Portuguese in the 1580s to guard the harbor.

name: Baku
fact: The Heydar Aliyev Center, with its flowing curves and almost no straight lines, was designed by Zaha Hadid and opened in 2012.

name: Tbilisi
fact: The city's name comes from the Georgian word for warm, after the sulfur hot springs of Abanotubani.

name: Yerevan
fact: The city grew around Erebuni, a fortress founded in 782 BC, which makes it older than Rome.

name: Sydney
fact: Jorn Utzon, the Danish architect of the city's Opera House, left the project in 1966 and never saw his building finished.

name: Melbourne
fact: The Royal Exhibition Building, built for the International Exhibition of 1880, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Canberra
fact: The city was designed by the Chicago architects Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin, who won an international competition in 1912.

name: Auckland
fact: The city is built on a volcanic field of around 50 volcanoes, Mount Eden among them.

name: Wellington
fact: The Beehive, the executive wing of the parliament buildings, is named for its shape.

name: New York
fact: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from the people of France and was dedicated in 1886.

name: Washington
fact: Every US president since John Adams has lived in the White House.

name: San Francisco
fact: The Golden Gate Bridge is painted a color called International Orange.

name: Los Angeles
fact: The Hollywood Sign was put up in 1923 to advertise a housing development and originally read 'Hollywoodland'.

name: Chicago
fact: Willis Tower was called the Sears Tower until it was renamed in 2009.

name: Las Vegas
fact: Most of the famous casinos on the Strip actually lie outside the city limits, in the unincorporated town of Paradise.

name: New Orleans
fact: Despite its name, most of the French Quarter's old buildings are Spanish colonial, rebuilt after great fires in 1788 and 1794.

name: Boston
fact: The tall left-field wall at Fenway Park is nicknamed the Green Monster.

name: Seattle
fact: The Space Needle was built for the 1962 World's Fair.

name: Miami
fact: The Art Deco district of South Beach has one of the largest collections of Art Deco buildings in the world.

name: Philadelphia
fact: Both the Declaration of Independence and the US Constitution were debated and signed in Independence Hall.

name: Toronto
fact: The CN Tower was the tallest free-standing structure in the world for more than three decades.

name: Montreal
fact: Habitat 67, a stack of concrete boxes designed by Moshe Safdie, was built for the 1967 World's Fair, Expo 67.

name: Vancouver
fact: Stanley Park is larger than New York's Central Park.

name: Quebec City
fact: It is the only city in the Americas north of Mexico whose old fortified walls still stand.

name: Ottawa
fact: In winter a 7.8-kilometre stretch of the Rideau Canal is turned into a skating rink, the Rideau Canal Skateway.

name: Mexico City
fact: The city is built on the drained bed of Lake Texcoco, on top of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan.

name: Havana
fact: A huge steel outline of Che Guevara's face looks down on the Plaza de la Revolución from the Interior Ministry building.

name: Rio de Janeiro
fact: Christ the Redeemer was completed in 1931 on the summit of Corcovado mountain.

name: Sao Paulo
fact: The MASP art museum's main gallery hangs from two red concrete beams, leaving an open square beneath it.

name: Brasilia
fact: Built from scratch and inaugurated as the capital in 1960, the city follows Lucio Costa's plan in the shape of an airplane.

name: Salvador
fact: The Lacerda Elevator, opened in 1873, carries people between the city's lower town and upper town.

name: Buenos Aires
fact: Eva Peron is buried in Recoleta Cemetery, in her family's Duarte tomb.

name: Santiago

landmarks.n: Museum of Memory and Human Rights

fact: The 300-metre Gran Torre in the Costanera Center was the tallest building in South America when it was completed.

name: Lima
fact: Huaca Pucllana is an adobe pyramid about 1,500 years old, now surrounded by the apartment blocks of Miraflores.

name: Cusco
fact: The Spanish built a convent on top of the Inca temple Qorikancha, and its Inca stone walls have outlasted earthquakes that wrecked the colonial building.

name: Bogota
fact: The Gold Museum holds the world's largest collection of pre-Hispanic gold objects.

name: Cartagena
fact: Castillo San Felipe de Barajas helped the city hold out against a huge British siege in 1741.

name: Quito
fact: Instead of gargoyles, the Basilica del Voto Nacional is decorated with stone animals native to Ecuador, such as tortoises and iguanas.

name: La Paz
fact: Mi Teleferico, whose first lines opened in 2014, is a network of cable cars used as everyday public transport between La Paz and El Alto.

name: Montevideo
fact: Estadio Centenario hosted the final of the first FIFA World Cup in 1930.

name: Panama City
fact: The Biomuseo was the first building in Latin America designed by Frank Gehry.

name: Cairo
fact: The Hanging Church takes its name from being built on top of a gatehouse of the Roman fortress of Babylon.

name: Luxor
fact: The city stands on the site of ancient Thebes, Egypt's capital during much of the New Kingdom.

name: Alexandria
fact: The Citadel of Qaitbay was built in the 15th century on the site of the ancient Pharos lighthouse.

name: Aswan
fact: Philae Temple was taken apart and rebuilt on Agilkia Island to save it from the rising waters behind the dams.

name: Marrakesh
fact: The Majorelle Garden was bought and restored by the fashion designer Yves Saint Laurent and his partner Pierre Berge.

name: Fez
fact: Founded in 859, Al-Qarawiyyin is often called the oldest continuously operating university in the world.

name: Casablanca
fact: Part of the Hassan II Mosque stands over the Atlantic Ocean, and its minaret is one of the tallest in the world.

name: Rabat
fact: Hassan Tower is the minaret of a great mosque begun in the 12th century and never finished.

name: Tunis
fact: The Bardo Museum holds one of the largest collections of Roman mosaics in the world.

name: Cape Town
fact: Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 years in prison on Robben Island.

name: Johannesburg
fact: Two Nobel Peace Prize winners, Nelson Mandela and Desmond Tutu, had homes on Vilakazi Street in Soweto.

name: Nairobi
fact: The city has a national park inside its limits, where giraffes, lions and rhinos roam with skyscrapers in view.

name: Zanzibar City
fact: Freddie Mercury, the singer of Queen, was born in Stone Town in 1946.

name: Addis Ababa
fact: The fossil skeleton known as Lucy is kept in the city's National Museum.

name: Dakar
fact: The 49-metre bronze African Renaissance Monument, unveiled in 2010, stands on one of the twin Mamelles hills.

name: Accra
fact: Kwame Nkrumah, who led Ghana to independence in 1957, is buried in the mausoleum in the city's Memorial Park.

name: Lagos
fact: Third Mainland Bridge was the longest bridge in Africa when it opened in 1990.

name: Kigali
fact: The Hotel des Mille Collines sheltered more than a thousand people during the 1994 genocide, a story told in the film Hotel Rwanda.
